title: The Sunday Read: ‘Why We Take Animal Voyages’

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举办的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Sam Anderson.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是萨姆·安德森。

sentences.en: I'm a staff writer for the New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报杂志》的特约撰稿人。

sentences.en: I live up in the Hudson Valley, north of New York City, with my family and my two very hairy dogs, Walnut and Pistachio.
sentences.zh: 我和家人以及两只毛茸茸的狗——核桃和开心果，住在纽约市以北的哈德逊河谷。

sentences.en: I'm really lucky I get to follow my interests.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运能追随自己的兴趣。

sentences.en: And that means that I have written a good amount over the years about animals.
sentences.zh: 这意味着多年来我写了不少关于动物的文章。

sentences.en: I've written essays about the last two northern white rhinos in Kenya.
sentences.zh: 我写过关于肯尼亚最后两头北白犀的随笔。

sentences.en: I've written about why we watch animal videos online.
sentences.zh: 我写过关于我们为什么在网上看动物视频的文章。

sentences.en: So the magazine does an annual voyages issue.
sentences.zh: 杂志社每年都会出一期“旅行特刊”。

sentences.en: It's devoted to travel and we always get these spectacular photo essays from places all over the world.
sentences.zh: 它专注于旅行，我们总是能收到来自世界各地壮观的摄影专题。

sentences.en: And this year was a little different than usual.
sentences.zh: 而今年有些不同寻常。

sentences.en: We decided to focus on animal voyages.
sentences.zh: 我们决定聚焦于“动物之旅”。

sentences.en: We asked some photographers for kind of dream trips that they'd always wanted to take that involved animals.
sentences.zh: 我们询问了一些摄影师，了解他们一直想进行的、与动物有关的梦想之旅。

sentences.en: Six photographers got sent all over the world.
sentences.zh: 六位摄影师被派往世界各地。

sentences.en: They went to Iceland, South Korea, French Guiana, Bolivia, Ghana, and to some zoos in the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们去了冰岛、韩国、法属圭亚那、玻利维亚、加纳，以及美国的一些动物园。

sentences.en: And because I love animals, I was roped into helping design the issue.
sentences.zh: 因为我热爱动物，我也被拉来帮忙设计这一期内容。

sentences.en: I'll be reading the introduction that I wrote for the issue, which is about why we take animal voyages.
sentences.zh: 我将朗读我为这一期撰写的引言，内容是关于我们为什么要进行动物之旅。

sentences.en: And if you're listening to this, go find an animal to pet.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在听这段音频，快去找只动物摸摸吧。

sentences.en: I have a ridiculous dog named Walnut.
sentences.zh: 我有一只滑稽的狗，叫核桃。

sentences.en: He is as domesticated as a beast can be.
sentences.zh: 他是一只被驯化得不能再彻底的野兽。

sentences.en: A purebred, long-haired, miniature dachshund with fur so thick it feels rich and creamy, like pudding.
sentences.zh: 一只纯种的长毛迷你腊肠犬，毛发浓密，摸起来像布丁一样丰富而细腻。

sentences.en: His tail is a huge, spreading, golden fan, a clutch of sunbeaMs. He looks less like a dog than like a tropical fish.
sentences.zh: 他的尾巴像一把巨大的、散开的金色扇子，像一簇阳光。比起狗，他看起来更像一条热带鱼。

sentences.en: People see him and gasp.
sentences.zh: 人们看到他都会惊呼。

sentences.en: Sometimes I tell Walnut, right out loud, that he is my precious little teddy bear, pudding cup, sweet boy, snuggle stinker.
sentences.zh: 有时我会大声对核桃说，他是我的珍宝小泰迪熊、布丁杯、甜心男孩、爱蹭人的小臭蛋。

sentences.en: In my daily life, Walnut is omnipresent.
sentences.zh: 在我的日常生活中，核桃无处不在。

sentences.en: He shadows me all over the house.
sentences.zh: 他在屋子里到处跟着我。

sentences.en: When I sit, he gallops up into my lap.
sentences.zh: 当我坐下时，他会飞奔到我的膝盖上。

sentences.en: When I go to bed, he stretches out his long, warm body against my body.
sentences.zh: 当我上床睡觉时，他会把长长的、温暖的身体贴着我的身体伸展开来。

sentences.en: Or he tucks himself under my chin, like a soft violin.
sentences.zh: 或者他会像一把柔软的小提琴一样缩在我的下巴下面。

sentences.en: Walnut is so relentlessly present that sometimes, paradoxically, he disappears.
sentences.zh: 核桃的存在感如此强烈，以至于有时，矛盾的是，他反而消失了。

sentences.en: If I'm stressed or tired, I can go a whole day without noticing him.
sentences.zh: 如果我感到压力或疲惫，我可能一整天都不会注意到他。

sentences.en: I will pet him idly.
sentences.zh: 我会漫不经心地抚摸他。

sentences.en: I will yell at him, absentmindedly, for barking at the mailman.
sentences.zh: 我会心不在焉地对他大喊大叫，因为他对着邮递员吠叫。

sentences.en: I will nuzzle him with my foot, but I won't really see him.
sentences.zh: 我会用脚蹭他，但我并没有真正地“看见”他。

sentences.en: He will ask for my attention, but I will have no attention to give.
sentences.zh: 他会寻求我的关注，但我却无暇顾及。

sentences.en: Humans are notorious for this, for our ability to become blind to our surroundings, even a fluffy little jewel of a mammal, like Walnut.
sentences.zh: 人类以这种能力而闻名，即对周围环境变得视而不见，即使是像核桃这样毛茸茸的、如宝石般的小哺乳动物也不例外。

sentences.en: John Berger, the brilliant
sentences.zh: 约翰·伯格，那位才华横溢的

sentences.en: British artist critic, could have been writing about all of this when he lamented, 45 years ago, modern humanity's impoverished relationship to animals.
sentences.zh: 英国艺术评论家，在45年前感叹现代人类与动物之间贫乏的关系时，或许就是在写这一切。

sentences.en: In the last two centuries, he wrote, animals have gradually disappeared.
sentences.zh: 他写道，在过去的两个世纪里，动物已经逐渐消失了。

sentences.en: Today, we live without them.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们生活在没有它们的世界里。

sentences.en: On its face, this claim is ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 表面上看，这种说法很荒谬。

sentences.en: Animals are everywhere in modern life.
sentences.zh: 动物在现代生活中随处可见。

sentences.en: More of us own pets than at any other time in human history.
sentences.zh: 我们中拥有宠物的人数比人类历史上任何时候都多。

sentences.en: We can drive to zoos, cat cafes, national parks, wildlife sanctuaries.
sentences.zh: 我们可以开车去动物园、猫咪咖啡馆、国家公园、野生动物保护区。

sentences.en: We can lie in bed and share viral TikToks of buffaloes grunting, puppies howling, parrots taunting hungry cats.
sentences.zh: 我们可以躺在床上分享 TikTok 上水牛咕哝、小狗嚎叫、鹦鹉嘲弄饥饿猫咪的病毒式视频。

sentences.en: We can watch live feeds on our tiny phones of eagles incubating eggs, or drone footage of polar bears hunting seals on 50-foot iMac screens.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在小小的手机上观看老鹰孵蛋的直播，或者在50英寸的 iMac 屏幕上观看无人机拍摄的北极熊捕食海豹的画面。

sentences.en: But Berger would argue that these things are all just symptoms of our lost intimacy with animals.
sentences.zh: 但伯格会认为，这些都只是我们与动物失去亲密关系的症状。

sentences.en: None of them represent meaningful, old-fashioned contact.
sentences.zh: 它们都不代表有意义的、老派的接触。

sentences.en: Since the primordial beginnings of our species, he writes, animals have been integral to human life.
sentences.zh: 他写道，自我们物种起源之初，动物就一直是人类生活中不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: Animals constituted the first circle of what surrounded man, according to Berger.
sentences.zh: 据伯格所言，动物构成了环绕人类的第一个圈子。

sentences.en: He goes on, perhaps that already suggests too great a distance.
sentences.zh: 他继续说道，也许这已经暗示了太大的距离。

sentences.en: They were with man at the center of his world.
sentences.zh: 它们曾与人类一起处于世界的中心。

sentences.en: Animals were not only predators and prey, they were myths, symbols, companions, peers, teachers, guides.
sentences.zh: 动物不仅是捕食者和猎物，它们还是神话、象征、伙伴、同伴、导师和向导。

sentences.en: The patterns of their movement defined the edges of the human world.
sentences.zh: 它们移动的模式定义了人类世界的边缘。

sentences.en: Their shapes defined the stars.
sentences.zh: 它们的形状定义了星辰。

sentences.en: They made human life possible.
sentences.zh: 它们使人类的生活成为可能。

sentences.en: A few ostrich eggs could sustain hunter-gatherers for days.
sentences.zh: 几枚鸵鸟蛋就能维持狩猎采集者几天的生存。

sentences.en: First as food, then as water carriers that enabled them to cross vast, parched distances.
sentences.zh: 最初作为食物，后来作为运水工具，使他们能够穿越广袤、干旱的距离。

sentences.en: We all know what happened next.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: Capitalism, industrialization, urbanization, the internal combustion engine, suburban sprawl, fast food, chicken nuggets, factory farMs. Animals, our sharp,
sentences.zh: 资本主义、工业化、城市化、内燃机、郊区扩张、快餐、鸡块、工厂化农场。动物，我们那些敏锐、

sentences.en: loud, restless, dangerous, inconvenient planetary roommates, were pushed to the margins.
sentences.zh: 吵闹、不安分、危险、不方便的行星室友，被推到了边缘。

sentences.en: For Berger, this was a profound loss, not only for the subjugated animals, but also for the humans who did the subjugating.
sentences.zh: 对伯格来说，这不仅是被征服动物的巨大损失，也是那些进行征服的人类的损失。

sentences.en: The animal has secrets which, unlike the secrets of caves, mountains, seas, are specifically addressed to man, he writes.
sentences.zh: 他写道，动物拥有秘密，这些秘密与洞穴、山脉、海洋的秘密不同，它们是专门针对人类的。

sentences.en: With their parallel lives, animals offer man a companionship, which is different from any offered by human exchange.
sentences.zh: 凭借它们平行的生命，动物为人类提供了一种陪伴，这与人类交流所提供的任何陪伴都不同。

sentences.en: Different because it is a companionship offered to the loneliness of man as a species.
sentences.zh: 之所以不同，是因为这种陪伴是提供给作为物种的人类的孤独感的。

sentences.en: Our lost closeness with animals, ushered in a sharp existential pain.
sentences.zh: 我们与动物失去的亲密关系，引发了一种尖锐的生存痛苦。

sentences.en: A state of beastly alienation.
sentences.zh: 一种野兽般的异化状态。

sentences.en: Modern humans can try to rationalize that loss in infinite ways.
sentences.zh: 现代人类可以尝试用无数种方式来合理化这种损失。

sentences.en: Is it such a bad thing that most of us no longer have to worry about wolf packs stealing our leftover caribou meat?
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人不再需要担心狼群偷走我们剩下的驯鹿肉，这难道不是一件好事吗？

sentences.en: We can concoct all kinds of synthetic replacements.
sentences.zh: 我们可以炮制各种合成替代品。

sentences.en: Ant farms, sea monkeys, pet rocks, chia pets, tamagotchis.
sentences.zh: 蚂蚁农场、海猴子、宠物石、奇亚宠物、电子宠物。

sentences.en: Growing up, I fell in love with a battery-powered robot owl named Hootbot.
sentences.zh: 我小时候爱上了一个叫 Hootbot 的电池驱动机器人猫头鹰。

sentences.en: We can sit at home with our pets in our laps, clicking on animal videos, laughing and crying, and forwarding them to our friends.
sentences.zh: 我们可以坐在家里，让宠物趴在膝盖上，点击动物视频，又笑又哭，并转发给朋友。

sentences.en: But none of these will fill the creaturely hole at the center of human life.
sentences.zh: 但这些都无法填补人类生活中心那个生物性的空洞。

sentences.en: They're not even close to the same shape.
sentences.zh: 它们甚至连形状都不一样。

sentences.en: We will continue to feel that loss, to yearn for those parallel lives, for the ancient strangeness of animal familiarity.
sentences.zh: 我们将继续感受到那种损失，渴望那些平行的生命，渴望动物熟悉感中那古老的陌生感。

sentences.en: If necessary, we will search the world for it.
sentences.zh: 如果有必要，我们将走遍世界去寻找它。

sentences.en: And so, sometimes, we head out on an animal voyage.
sentences.zh: 所以，有时我们会踏上一场动物之旅。

sentences.en: We take ourselves off to a place that is still wild, or where wildness has been carefully curated, or simulated, or reintroduced.
sentences.zh: 我们把自己带到一个仍然野性十足的地方，或者野性被精心策划、模拟或重新引入的地方。

sentences.en: We can visit squirrel monkeys, for instance, at an abandoned penal colony in French Guiana.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们可以去法属圭亚那的一个废弃流放地探访松鼠猴。

sentences.en: We can watch strange, hairy horses galloping around near Icelandic volcanoes.
sentences.zh: 我们可以观看奇怪的多毛马在冰岛火山附近奔跑。

sentences.en: We can climb up into the lush tree canopies of Ghana to stare at the rosy bee-eaters.
sentences.zh: 我们可以爬上加纳郁郁葱葱的树冠，凝视玫瑰蜂虎。

sentences.en: Wherever we go, our goal will be roughly the same—to put our own animal bodies near the bodies of the creatures we have pushed away—to effect an existential reunion.
sentences.zh: 无论我们去哪里，我们的目标大致相同——将我们自己的动物身体靠近那些被我们推开的生物的身体——以实现一场存在主义的重逢。

sentences.en: If that sounds mystical, well, it is.
sentences.zh: 如果这听起来很神秘，嗯，它确实是。

sentences.en: It's hard to put into words exactly what we're looking for when we go out to meet a distant animal.
sentences.zh: 很难用语言准确表达当我们去见一种遥远的动物时，我们到底在寻找什么。

sentences.en: The need, probably, goes deeper than language.
sentences.zh: 这种需求，可能比语言更深层。

sentences.en: On some level, I think we're looking to orient ourselves, to locate ourselves on an accurate map of the universe.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我认为我们是在寻找定位自己，在宇宙的精确地图上找到自己的位置。

sentences.en: Not using the coordinates we've been handed by human culture—the self-flattering, narcissistic, anthropocentric fantasies of a world made for us, in our image.
sentences.zh: 不是使用人类文化交给我们的坐标——那些以自我为中心、自恋的、人类中心主义的幻想，即世界是为我们、按我们的形象创造的。

sentences.en: Something in us yearns for accuracy.
sentences.zh: 我们内心深处渴望准确。

sentences.en: Even if it comes at the price of a demotion, it is liberating to be decentered.
sentences.zh: 即使是以被降级为代价，去中心化也是一种解放。

sentences.en: And animals, always, are happy to perform this service.
sentences.zh: 而动物，总是乐于提供这项服务。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费探索《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall, to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: An animal voyage is special because it requires us to make many journeys all at once.
sentences.zh: 动物之旅之所以特别，是因为它要求我们同时进行多种旅程。

sentences.en: To really connect with another creature, you have to cross multiple kinds of
sentences.zh: 要真正与另一种生物建立联系，你必须跨越多种

sentences.en: distance—physical, spiritual, temporal.
sentences.zh: 距离——物理的、精神的、时间的。

sentences.en: You have to leave our daily sense of clock time and reach into something like evolutionary time.
sentences.zh: 你必须离开我们日常的时钟时间感，触及某种类似进化时间的东西。

sentences.en: You have to stare across vast chasms of consciousness.
sentences.zh: 你必须凝视意识的巨大鸿沟。

sentences.en: Look into the eye of a bison, a marlin, a parrot, an iguana.
sentences.zh: 看着野牛、马林鱼、鹦鹉、鬣蜥的眼睛。

sentences.en: What is the gulf between your mind and theirs?
sentences.zh: 你的思想和它们的思想之间存在着怎样的鸿沟？

sentences.en: That space can't be measured in miles or light years or any other unit we can name.
sentences.zh: 那个空间无法用英里、光年或我们能命名的任何其他单位来衡量。

sentences.en: It will probably never be definitively crossed.
sentences.zh: 它可能永远不会被彻底跨越。

sentences.en: What kind of bridge would ever even begin to work?
sentences.zh: 什么样的桥梁才能开始发挥作用呢？

sentences.en: And so an animal voyage is, on some level, always destined to fail.
sentences.zh: 因此，动物之旅在某种程度上注定是要失败的。

sentences.en: This, too, is part of its appeal.
sentences.zh: 这也是它吸引力的一部分。

sentences.en: My favorite record of an animal voyage is a book that's fluent in failure.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的动物之旅记录是一本精通失败的书。

sentences.en: Peter Matheson's nonfiction masterpiece, The Snow Leopard, chronicles a truly extreme animal queSt. In 1973, Matheson spent
sentences.zh: 彼得·马西森的非虚构杰作《雪豹》，记录了一场真正极端的动物探索。1973年，马西森花了

sentences.en: two months trekking into the Himalayas with his biologist friend George Schaller.
sentences.zh: 两个月时间与他的生物学家朋友乔治·夏勒徒步进入喜马拉雅山脉。

sentences.en: They were hoping to glimpse one of the world's most impressive and elusive animals—a powerful cat so rare that Schaller
sentences.zh: 他们希望能瞥见世界上最令人印象深刻且难以捉摸的动物之一——一种极其罕见的强大猫科动物，以至于夏勒

sentences.en: knew of only one Westerner, aside from himself, who had seen one in the past quarter century.
sentences.zh: 知道除了他自己之外，在过去四分之一个世纪里，只有一位西方人见过它。

sentences.en: According to
sentences.zh: 据

sentences.en: Matheson, the snow leopard is a near-mythic beast that has the power to watch its watchers while remaining nearly invisible.
sentences.zh: 马西森说，雪豹是一种近乎神话的野兽，它有能力在保持近乎隐形的同时观察观察者。

sentences.en: One can stare straight at it from yards away, he writes, and fail to see it.
sentences.zh: 他写道，一个人可以在几码外直视它，却看不见它。

sentences.en: Matheson's journey is brutal, dangerous, and disorienting—emotionally and physically exhausting.
sentences.zh: 马西森的旅程是残酷、危险且令人迷失方向的——在情感和身体上都令人筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: He hikes along perilous ledges.
sentences.zh: 他在危险的岩架上徒步。

sentences.en: His guides suffer bouts of snow blindness.
sentences.zh: 他的向导遭受了雪盲症的折磨。

sentences.en: Matheson weathers freezing temperatures in a tent so small he can't even sit up.
sentences.zh: 马西森在一个小到连坐都坐不直的帐篷里忍受着冰冻的温度。

sentences.en: All along, he has much more on his mind than wildlife.
sentences.zh: 一直以来，他脑子里想的远不止野生动物。

sentences.en: Early in the book, we learn that Matheson's wife has recently died of cancer, and that he has left his young son at home to make this pilgrimage.
sentences.zh: 在书的开头，我们得知马西森的妻子最近死于癌症，他把年幼的儿子留在家里去进行这次朝圣。

sentences.en: He later told an interviewer that he drafted the book by hand, on the trek itself, day by day, as a zen practice of close observation.
sentences.zh: 他后来告诉一位采访者，他是作为一种近距离观察的禅修练习，在徒步过程中逐日手写完成了这本书。

sentences.en: Matheson and his wife were both serious students of Buddhism.
sentences.zh: 马西森和他的妻子都是认真的佛教学生。

sentences.en: This gives the writing a strange, elevated, living quality that few books ever approach.
sentences.zh: 这赋予了这部作品一种罕见的、崇高的、鲜活的品质，很少有书能达到这种境界。

sentences.en: Matheson was a devoted environmentalist, prone to raging at human excesses, and his voyage begins in a fallen world, a region already devastated
sentences.zh: 马西森是一位忠诚的环保主义者，容易对人类的过度行为感到愤怒，他的旅程始于一个堕落的世界，一个已经被

sentences.en: by overpopulation and pollution, where animals that used to be common—elephants, tigers, rhinos, cheetahs—have all been driven away.
sentences.zh: 人口过剩和污染摧毁的地区，在那里，曾经常见的动物——大象、老虎、犀牛、猎豹——都已被驱逐。

sentences.en: We have outsmarted ourselves like greedy monkeys, and now we are full of dread, he writes.
sentences.zh: 他写道，我们像贪婪的猴子一样自作聪明，现在我们充满了恐惧。

sentences.en: He climbs higher and higher, away from civilization, toward an ancient Tibetan sacred site known as Crystal Mountain.
sentences.zh: 他越爬越高，远离文明，朝着一个被称为“水晶山”的古老西藏圣地前进。

sentences.en: Along the way, he sits and meditates.
sentences.zh: 一路上，他坐下来冥想。

sentences.en: He stops at Buddhist shrines.
sentences.zh: 他在佛教神龛前停下。

sentences.en: He is overwhelmed by feelings.
sentences.zh: 他被各种情绪淹没了。

sentences.en: As the altitude rises, Matheson's style burns itself down to stark poetry.
sentences.zh: 随着海拔升高，马西森的文风燃烧成了纯粹的诗歌。

sentences.en: There is no wisp of cloud, he writes.
sentences.zh: 他写道，没有一丝云彩。

sentences.en: Clear, clear, clear, clear.
sentences.zh: 清澈，清澈，清澈，清澈。

sentences.en: He begins to merge with the landscape.
sentences.zh: 他开始与景观融为一体。

sentences.en: As he puts it, I grow into these mountains like a moss.
sentences.zh: 正如他所说，我像苔藓一样长进了这些山脉里。

sentences.en: And he detaches from linear time, writing,
sentences.zh: 他脱离了线性时间，写道，

sentences.en: Simultaneously, I am myself, the child I was, the old man I will be.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我既是我自己，也是曾经的那个孩子，更是未来那个老去的我。

sentences.en: He has visions,
sentences.zh: 他有幻象，

sentences.en: hallucinatory epiphanies.
sentences.zh: 那是幻觉般的顿悟。

sentences.en: Sometimes when I meditate, he writes, the big rocks dance.
sentences.zh: 他写道，有时当我冥想时，巨大的岩石会跳起舞来。

sentences.en: On his voyage,
sentences.zh: 在他的旅途中，

sentences.en: Matheson encounters all kinds of animals—yaks, goats, lizards, frogs, roosters, horses.
sentences.zh: 马西森遇到了各种各样的动物——牦牛、山羊、蜥蜴、青蛙、公鸡、马。

sentences.en: He sees a lone red panda, and many clusters of blue sheep, and even a pack of wolves.
sentences.zh: 他看到了一只落单的小熊猫，许多成群的岩羊，甚至还有一群狼。

sentences.en: In a tiny village, he is attacked by a dog.
sentences.zh: 在一个小村庄里，他遭到了一只狗的袭击。

sentences.en: He beats it off with a stick.
sentences.zh: 他用棍子把它赶走了。

sentences.en: But where is the snow leopard?
sentences.zh: 但雪豹在哪里呢？

sentences.en: Nowhere and everywhere.
sentences.zh: 无处不在，又无处可寻。

sentences.en: Up near
sentences.zh: 在靠近

sentences.en: Crystal Mountain, as time stretches toward eternity, Matheson sees tantalizing traces of the great creature.
sentences.zh: 水晶山的地方，随着时间向永恒延伸，马西森看到了这种伟大生物留下的诱人痕迹。

sentences.en: Scat, scratch marks.
sentences.zh: 粪便，抓痕。

sentences.en: The blue sheep huddle nervously, suggesting the presence of an apex predator.
sentences.zh: 岩羊紧张地挤在一起，暗示着顶级捕食者的存在。

sentences.en: Matheson speaks with a llama who claims to see snow leopards frequently.
sentences.zh: 马西森与一位声称经常见到雪豹的喇嘛交谈。

sentences.en: He finds snow leopard paw prints, fresh as petals, on the trail.
sentences.zh: 他在小径上发现了雪豹的脚印，像花瓣一样新鲜。

sentences.en: He strains his attention so hard that it inflects everything around him.
sentences.zh: 他如此专注，以至于这种专注影响了他周围的一切。

sentences.en: It is wonderful, he writes, how the presence of this creature draws the whole landscape to a point, from the glint of light on the old horns of a sheep to the ring of a pebble
sentences.zh: 他写道，这种生物的存在将整个景观聚焦于一点，这真是奇妙，从羊角上闪烁的光芒到鹅卵石的敲击声，

sentences.en: on the frozen ground.
sentences.zh: 在冰冻的地面上。

sentences.en: Toward the end of his trip, Matheson finds that a leopard has made its scrape right in my boot print, as if in sign that I am not to leave.
sentences.zh: 在旅程快结束时，马西森发现一只雪豹正好在他的靴印上留下了抓痕，仿佛在示意我不该离开。

sentences.en: And yet he has to leave.
sentences.zh: 然而他不得不离开。

sentences.en: Down below, his life waits for him.
sentences.zh: 在山下，他的生活在等着他。

sentences.en: The great perfect shock of the snow leopard, and stop listening if you need to, because here comes a spoiler, is that Matheson never actually sees a snow leopard.
sentences.zh: 雪豹带来的巨大而完美的震撼——如果你需要的话可以停止收听，因为接下来要剧透了——就是马西森实际上从未见过雪豹。

sentences.en: The animal in the book's title, The Whole Reason for the Journey, refuses to put itself on display.
sentences.zh: 书名中的这种动物，即这趟旅程的全部意义所在，拒绝让自己现身。

sentences.en: This failure becomes a powerful lesson in loss, a chance to meditate on the tangled nature of visibility and invisibility.
sentences.zh: 这种失败变成了一堂关于失落的深刻课程，一个沉思可见与不可见之间纠葛本质的机会。

sentences.en: If the snow leopard should manifest itself, then I am ready to see the snow leopard, Matheson writes.
sentences.zh: 马西森写道，如果雪豹应该显现，那么我已经准备好去见它了。

sentences.en: If not, then somehow, and I don't understand this instinct, even now, I am not ready to perceive it, in the same way that I am not ready to resolve my koan.
sentences.zh: 如果没有，那么不知何故——即使到现在，我也不明白这种直觉——我还没有准备好去感知它，就像我还没有准备好参透我的公案一样。

sentences.en: And in the not-seeing, I am content.
sentences.zh: 而在这种“未见”之中，我感到满足。

sentences.en: I think I must be disappointed, having come so far, and yet I do not feel that way.
sentences.zh: 我想我本该感到失望，毕竟走了这么远，但我并没有那种感觉。

sentences.en: I am disappointed, and also, I am not disappointed.
sentences.zh: 我感到失望，同时，我又不感到失望。

sentences.en: That the snow leopard is, that it is here, that its frosty eyes watch us from the mountain.
sentences.zh: 雪豹的存在，它就在这里，它那冰冷的双眼从山上注视着我们。

sentences.en: That is enough.
sentences.zh: 这就足够了。

sentences.en: Even Schaller, the hardened scientist, summons a bit of poetry.
sentences.zh: 就连坚毅的科学家夏勒，也流露出一丝诗意。

sentences.en: You know something, he says to Matheson?
sentences.zh: 他对马西森说，你知道吗？

sentences.en: We've seen so much.
sentences.zh: 我们已经见识过太多了。

sentences.en: Maybe it's better if there are some things that we don't see.
sentences.zh: 也许有些东西我们看不见会更好。

sentences.en: Today, nearly 50 years later, if you are so inclined, you can go see a snow leopard at the zoo.
sentences.zh: 今天，近50年过去了，如果你有兴趣，你可以去动物园看雪豹。

sentences.en: According to the Snow Leopard Conservancy, approximately 600 of them live at accredited zoos worldwide.
sentences.zh: 据雪豹保护协会称，全球有认证的动物园里大约生活着600只雪豹。

sentences.en: Biologically, it is the same animal that Matheson was seeking.
sentences.zh: 从生物学上讲，它和马西森寻找的是同一种动物。

sentences.en: And yet, it's hard to imagine a more different kind of encounter, or one that Matheson, with his cynical tendencies, might have been less interested in.
sentences.zh: 然而，很难想象还有比这更不同的相遇方式，或者说，以马西森那种愤世嫉俗的倾向，他可能对这种相遇最不感兴趣。

sentences.en: I long to see the snow leopard, he wrote, yet to glimpse it by camera flash, at night, crouched on a bait, is not to see it.
sentences.zh: 他写道，我渴望见到雪豹，但通过夜间的相机闪光灯，在诱饵旁瞥见它，那并不算真正见到它。

sentences.en: John Berger, too, was dismissive of zoos.
sentences.zh: 约翰·伯格也对动物园不屑一顾。

sentences.en: They were, for him, the apex of our alienation.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，那是我们异化的极致。

sentences.en: He wrote, you are looking at something that has been rendered absolutely marginal, and all the concentration you can muster will never be enough to centralize it.
sentences.zh: 他写道，你正在看一个被彻底边缘化的事物，无论你如何集中注意力，都永远无法让它回到中心。

sentences.en: Zoo animals, according to Berger, represented the living monument to their own disappearance.
sentences.zh: 在伯格看来，动物园里的动物代表了它们自身消失的活纪念碑。

sentences.en: And it's true that there is something uncanny about seeing a snow leopard sprawled behind glass, in an artificial habitat, in full view of families pushing strollers.
sentences.zh: 确实，看到一只雪豹在玻璃后、在人造栖息地里，在推着婴儿车的家庭众目睽睽之下懒散地躺着，有一种怪异的感觉。

sentences.en: But in a world where mass extinction is advancing exponentially, where the snow leopard's natural
sentences.zh: 但在一个大规模灭绝呈指数级增长的世界里，在一个雪豹的自然

sentences.en: habitat is being thawed and polluted, in a world like that, where else are these animals supposed to survive?
sentences.zh: 栖息地正在融化和污染的世界里，在这样的世界里，这些动物还能去哪里生存呢？

sentences.en: And how else are we supposed to see them?
sentences.zh: 我们还能通过什么方式见到它们呢？

sentences.en: Or should we simply surrender ourselves forever to the fate of non-seeing?
sentences.zh: 还是说我们应该彻底屈服于“看不见”的命运？

sentences.en: I have loved animals since I was a child.
sentences.zh: 我从小就喜欢动物。

sentences.en: My first word was bird.
sentences.zh: 我说的第一个词是“鸟”。

sentences.en: I ate dog food out of solidarity with my first pet.
sentences.zh: 为了声援我的第一只宠物，我甚至吃过狗粮。

sentences.en: I wanted to grow up to be a veterinarian or a zoologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我曾想长大后成为一名兽医或动物学家。

sentences.en: Writing derailed me.
sentences.zh: 写作让我偏离了轨道。

sentences.en: As an adult, I've been lucky to be able to take animal voyages all over the world.
sentences.zh: 成年后，我很幸运能去世界各地进行动物之旅。

sentences.en: I've swum with manatees in Florida, and sat on an Icelandic cliffside among thousands of puffins.
sentences.zh: 我在佛罗里达和海牛一起游泳，在冰岛的悬崖边和成千上万只海鹦坐在一起。

sentences.en: I've watched the famous tree-climbing goats of Morocco.
sentences.zh: 我观赏过摩洛哥著名的爬树山羊。

sentences.en: I've seen them perched, absurdly,
sentences.zh: 我看到它们荒谬地栖息在

sentences.en: 20 feet above the ground, in the branches, like huge, hairy, white fruit.
sentences.zh: 离地20英尺的树枝上，就像巨大、多毛、白色的果实。

sentences.en: I once got to spend a whole week with the last two northern white rhinos on Earth.
sentences.zh: 我曾有幸与地球上最后两头北白犀共度了一整周。

sentences.en: The best trips, like Peter Matheson's search for the snow leopard, find a way to make themselves permanent.
sentences.zh: 最好的旅行，就像彼得·马西森寻找雪豹的旅程一样，总能找到让自己永恒的方式。

sentences.en: A northern white rhinoceros will not come home with you, but your awe at the rhinoceros, your amazement and respect and appreciation, that is portable.
sentences.zh: 北白犀不会跟你回家，但你对犀牛的敬畏，你的惊叹、尊重和欣赏，这些是可以随身携带的。

sentences.en: You can apply it to your goldfish, to your children, to the chipmunk that lives under the stairs, to the citizens around you.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它应用到你的金鱼、你的孩子、住在楼梯下的花栗鼠，以及你周围的公民身上。

sentences.en: To return home from an animal voyage is to become yourself a new animal, living in your old habitat.
sentences.zh: 从动物之旅回到家，意味着你自己变成了一种新的动物，生活在旧的栖息地里。

sentences.en: It is to find yourself voyaging in your own home, waking up to the other creatures that were there all along, inching them from the margins back toward
sentences.zh: 这意味着你发现自己在自己的家里旅行，醒来后发现那些一直都在的其他生物，将它们从边缘拉回到

sentences.en: the center of your life, where they belong.
sentences.zh: 你生活的中心，那里才是它们所属的地方。

sentences.en: It is to remind yourself that being with an animal, any kind of animal, anywhere at all, is its own kind of voyage.
sentences.zh: 这意味着提醒自己，与动物在一起——任何种类的动物，在任何地方——本身就是一种旅行。

sentences.en: When I come home from a trip, Walnut gets very excited.
sentences.zh: 当我旅行回家时，核桃（Walnut）会非常兴奋。

sentences.en: He prances and hops and barks and sniffs me at the door.
sentences.zh: 他在门口欢蹦乱跳，吠叫着嗅我。

sentences.en: And the consciousness of all the wild creatures I've seen, the puffins, rhinos, manatees, ferrets, the weird hairy wet horses, come to life for me inside of my domestic dog.
sentences.zh: 而我所见过的所有野生生物的意识——海鹦、犀牛、海牛、雪貂、那些奇怪多毛湿漉漉的马——都在我的家养狗身上活了过来。

sentences.en: He is suddenly one of these unfamiliar animals.
sentences.zh: 他突然变成了这些陌生动物中的一员。

sentences.en: I can pet him with my full attention, with a full union of our two attentions.
sentences.zh: 我可以全神贯注地抚摸他，让我们两人的注意力完全融合在一起。

sentences.en: He is new to me, and I am new to him.
sentences.zh: 他对我来说是新的，我对他也一样。

sentences.en: We are new again, together.
sentences.zh: 我们在一起，焕然一新。

sentences.en: Even when he is horrible.
sentences.zh: 即使在他表现得很糟糕的时候也是如此。

sentences.en: The most annoying thing Walnut does, even worse than barking at the mailman, is the ritual of his evening drink.
sentences.zh: 核桃做过最烦人的事，甚至比对邮递员吠叫还烦人，就是他晚上的喝水仪式。

sentences.en: Every night, when I'm settled in bed, when I'm on the brink of sleep, Walnut will suddenly get very thirsty.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上，当我躺在床上，快要睡着的时候，核桃突然就会变得很渴。

sentences.en: If I go to bed at 10.30, Walnut will get thirsty at 11.
sentences.zh: 如果我10点半上床，核桃11点就会渴。

sentences.en: If I go to bed at midnight, he'll wake me up at 1.
sentences.zh: 如果我午夜上床，他会在1点把我叫醒。

sentences.en: I've found that the only way I cannot be mad about this is to treat this ritual as its own special kind of voyage.
sentences.zh: 我发现，唯一能让自己不为此生气的方法，就是把这个仪式当作一种特殊的旅行。

sentences.en: To try to experience it as if for the first time.
sentences.zh: 试着像第一次经历它那样去体验它。

sentences.en: If I'm open to it, my upstairs hallway contains an astonishing amount of life.
sentences.zh: 如果我敞开心扉，楼上的走廊里蕴含着惊人的生命力。

sentences.en: The evening drink goes something like this.
sentences.zh: 晚上的喝水仪式大概是这样的。

sentences.en: First, Walnut will stand on the edge of the bed, in a muscular, stout little stance, and he will wave his big, ridiculous
sentences.zh: 首先，核桃会站在床边，摆出一个肌肉发达、敦实的小姿势，然后在我脸上挥动他那巨大、滑稽的

sentences.en: fan tail in my face, creating enough of a breeze that I can't ignore it.
sentences.zh: 扇形尾巴，制造出我无法忽视的微风。

sentences.en: I will roll over and try to go back to sleep, but he won't let me.
sentences.zh: 我会翻个身试图继续睡觉，但他不会让我如愿。

sentences.en: He'll stamp his hairy front paws and wag harder.
sentences.zh: 他会跺着多毛的前爪，摇得更起劲。

sentences.en: Then add expressive noises from his snout.
sentences.zh: 然后从鼻子里发出富有表现力的声音。

sentences.en: Half whine, half breath.
sentences.zh: 一半是呜咽，一半是呼吸。

sentences.en: Hardly audible except to me.
sentences.zh: 除了我，几乎没人能听见。

sentences.en: And so I give up.
sentences.zh: 于是我放弃了。

sentences.en: I sit up and pivot and plant my feet on the floor.
sentences.zh: 我坐起来，转过身，双脚着地。

sentences.en: I'm hardly even awake yet.
sentences.zh: 我甚至还没完全清醒。

sentences.en: And I make a little basket of my arms, like a running back preparing to take a handoff.
sentences.zh: 我把双臂围成一个小篮子，就像准备接球的跑卫一样。

sentences.en: And Walnut pops his body right into that pocket, entrusting the long length of his vulnerable spine, a hazard of the dachshund breed, to the stretch of my right arm.
sentences.zh: 核桃直接跳进那个怀抱里，把他那脆弱的长脊椎——腊肠犬品种的隐患——托付给我右臂的支撑。

sentences.en: And then he hangs his furry front legs over my left.
sentences.zh: 然后他把毛茸茸的前腿搭在我的左臂上。

sentences.en: From this point on, we function as a unit, a fusion of man and dog.
sentences.zh: 从这一刻起，我们作为一个整体运作，人与狗的融合。

sentences.en: As I lift my weight from the bed, Walnut does a little hop, just to help me with gravity.
sentences.zh: 当我从床上起身时，核桃会轻轻一跳，帮我对抗重力。

sentences.en: And we set off down the narrow hall.
sentences.zh: 然后我们出发走下狭窄的走廊。

sentences.en: We are Odysseus on the wine-dark sea.
sentences.zh: 我们是酒色大海上奥德修斯。

sentences.en: Walnut is
sentences.zh: 核桃是

sentences.en: Odysseus.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯。

sentences.en: I am the ship.
sentences.zh: 我是那艘船。

sentences.en: All of evolution, all of the births and deaths since caveman times, since wolf times, that produced my ancestors and his, all the firelight and sneak attacks and tenderly offered
sentences.zh: 所有的进化，自穴居人时代、狼时代以来所有的生与死，造就了我的祖先和他的祖先，所有的篝火、偷袭和温柔提供的

sentences.en: scraps of meat, the cages and houses, the secret stretchy coils of German DNA.
sentences.zh: 碎肉，笼子和房子，德国基因里秘密的伸缩螺旋。

sentences.en: It has all come, finally, to this.
sentences.zh: 这一切，最终都归结于此。

sentences.en: A fully grown, exhausted human man.
sentences.zh: 一个成年、疲惫的人类男性。

sentences.en: A tiny, panting, goofy, harmless dog, walking down the hall together.
sentences.zh: 一只气喘吁吁、傻乎乎、无害的小狗，一起走在走廊里。

sentences.en: Even in the dark, Walnut will tilt his snout up at me.
sentences.zh: 即使在黑暗中，核桃也会把鼻子向上对着我。

sentences.en: Throw me a deep, happy look from his big black eyes.
sentences.zh: 用他那双大大的黑眼睛深情而快乐地看着我。

sentences.en: I can feel this happening, even when I can't see it.
sentences.zh: 即使看不见，我也能感觉到这一切正在发生。

sentences.en: And he will snuffle the air until I say nice words to him.
sentences.zh: 他会嗅着空气，直到我对他说些好听的话。

sentences.en: Okay, you fuzzy stinker.
sentences.zh: 好了，你这个毛茸茸的小臭蛋。

sentences.en: Let's go get your evening drink.
sentences.zh: 我们去喝晚上的水吧。

sentences.en: And then always, I will lower my face, and he will lick my nose.
sentences.zh: 然后总是这样，我会低下头，他会舔我的鼻子。

sentences.en: And his breath is so bad, his fetid snout wind.
sentences.zh: 他的口气真难闻，那股恶臭的鼻息。

sentences.en: It smells like a scoop of the primordial soup.
sentences.zh: 闻起来就像一勺原始汤。

sentences.en: It is not good in any way.
sentences.zh: 一点也不好闻。

sentences.en: And yet I love it.
sentences.zh: 但我还是爱它。

sentences.en: Walnut and I move down the hall together, step by bipedal step.
sentences.zh: 核桃和我一起走在走廊里，一步一个脚印。

sentences.en: One, two, three, four, tired man and thirsty friend.
sentences.zh: 一、二、三、四，疲惫的人和口渴的朋友。

sentences.en: And together, we pass the wildlife of the hallway, a moth, a spider on the ceiling, both of which my children will yell at me later to move outside.
sentences.zh: 我们一起经过走廊里的野生生物，一只飞蛾，天花板上的一只蜘蛛，后来我的孩子们会大声叫我把它们移到外面去。

sentences.en: And of course, each of these creatures could be its own voyage, its own portal to millions of years of history.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些生物中的每一个都可以是一次旅行，通往数百万年历史的门户。

sentences.en: But we can't stop to study them now.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在不能停下来研究它们。

sentences.en: We are passing my son's room.
sentences.zh: 我们经过我儿子的房间。

sentences.en: We can hear him murmuring words to his friends in a voice that sounds disturbingly like my own voice.
sentences.zh: 我们可以听到他用一种听起来令人不安地像我自己的声音，在和朋友们低语。

sentences.en: Deep sound waves rumbling over deep mammalian cords.
sentences.zh: 深沉的声波在深层的哺乳动物声带上隆隆作响。

sentences.en: And now we are passing my daughter's room, my sweet, nearly grown-up girl, who was so tiny when we brought Walnut home as a golden puppy.
sentences.zh: 现在我们经过我女儿的房间，我那甜美、快要长大的女孩，当我们把核桃作为一只金色的幼犬带回家时，她还那么小。

sentences.en: But now she's moving off to college.
sentences.zh: 但现在她要去上大学了。

sentences.en: In her room, she has a hamster she calls Acorn.
sentences.zh: 在她的房间里，她有一只叫“橡子”（Acorn）的仓鼠。

sentences.en: Another consciousness.
sentences.zh: 另一个意识。

sentences.en: Another portal to millions of years.
sentences.zh: 另一个通往数百万年的门户。

sentences.en: To ancient ancestors in China.
sentences.zh: 通往中国古代的祖先。

sentences.en: Nighttime scampering over deserts.
sentences.zh: 在沙漠上奔跑的夜晚。

sentences.en: But we move on.
sentences.zh: 但我们继续前行。

sentences.en: Behind us in the hallway comes a sudden galumphing.
sentences.zh: 走廊后面传来一阵突然的奔跑声。

sentences.en: It is yet another animal.
sentences.zh: 那是另一只动物。

sentences.en: Our other dog, Pistachio.
sentences.zh: 我们的另一只狗，开心果（Pistachio）。

sentences.en: He's getting up to see what's happening.
sentences.zh: 他起床来看看发生了什么。

sentences.en: He was sleeping too, but now he's following us.
sentences.zh: 他刚才也在睡觉，但现在他跟着我们。

sentences.en: Pistachio is the opposite of Walnut.
sentences.zh: 开心果和核桃截然不同。

sentences.en: A huge mutt we adopted from a shelter.
sentences.zh: 我们从收容所领养的一只大杂种狗。

sentences.en: A gangly, scraggly, garbage muppet.
sentences.zh: 一只笨拙、邋遢、像垃圾堆里的布偶。

sentences.en: His body welded together out of old mops and sandpaper with legs like stilts and an enormous block head.
sentences.zh: 他的身体是用旧拖把和砂纸焊接在一起的，腿像高跷，头大得像块砖。

sentences.en: And a tail so long that when he whips it in joy, constantly, he beats himself in the face.
sentences.zh: 尾巴长得离谱，当他高兴地不停甩动时，会打到自己的脸。

sentences.en: Pistachio unfolds himself from his sleepy curl, stands, trots, huffs, and stares after us with big human eyes.
sentences.zh: 开心果从睡梦中舒展开身体，站起来，小跑，喘气，用那双像人一样的大眼睛盯着我们。

sentences.en: Walnut ignores him.
sentences.zh: 核桃无视他。

sentences.en: Because with every step, he is sniffing the dark air ahead of us.
sentences.zh: 因为每走一步，他都在嗅着我们前方黑暗的空气。

sentences.en: Like a car probing a night road with headlights.
sentences.zh: 就像汽车用前灯探照着夜路一样。

sentences.en: And he knows we are approaching his water dish now.
sentences.zh: 他知道我们现在正靠近他的水碗。

sentences.en: He knows I am about to bend my body in half to set his four paws simultaneously down on the floor.
sentences.zh: 他知道我正要弯下腰，把他的四只爪子同时放到地板上。

sentences.en: He knows that he will slap the cool water with his tongue for 15 seconds before I pick him up again and we journey back down the hall.
sentences.zh: 他知道他会用舌头拍打凉水15秒，然后我再抱起他，我们再沿着走廊走回去。

sentences.en: And I find myself wondering, although of course it doesn't matter, if Walnut was even thirsty, or if we are just playing out a mutual script.
sentences.zh: 我不禁在想，虽然这当然无关紧要，胡桃当时到底渴不渴，还是说我们只是在演一出共同的剧本。

sentences.en: Or maybe, and who could blame him?
sentences.zh: 又或者，谁又能怪他呢？

sentences.en: He just felt like taking a trip.
sentences.zh: 他只是想出去逛逛。

sentences.en: This was written and narrated by Sam Anderson.
sentences.zh: 本文由萨姆·安德森撰写并讲述。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。
